ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, point O is the origin. The line $y=2x-1$ intersects the line $y=\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{3}{2}$ at point A. A perpendicular line to the x-axis is drawn through point A, with point B being the foot of the perpendicular. The x-coordinate of point C is $-1$, and point C lies on the line $y=2x-1$. Connect BC. What are the coordinates of point A?

ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Solve the system of equations: \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} y=2x-1 \\ y=\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{3}{2} \end{array} \right. \] to get \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x=2\\ y=3 \end{array} \right. \] Therefore, the coordinates of point A are $\boxed{(2,3)}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, point O is the origin. The line $y=2x-1$ intersects the line $y=\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{3}{2}$ at point A. A perpendicular line to the x-axis is drawn through point A, with point B being the foot of the perpendicular. The x-coordinate of point C is $-1$, and point C lies on the line $y=2x-1$. Connect BC. What are the coordinates of point A?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Solve the system of equations: \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} y=2x-1 \\ y=\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{3}{2} \end{array} \right. \] to get \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x=2\\ y=3 \end{array} \right. \] Therefore, the coordinates of point A are $\boxed{(2,3)}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, O is the origin, and there are two oblique straight lines intersecting at point A; a vertical line segment is drawn from point A to the x-axis, and the foot of the perpendicular is labeled B; point C is marked on the steeper oblique straight line, and B and C are also connected in the figure. Then reason: The problem states that point A is the intersection point of the line y=2x-1 and the line y=(3/4)x+3/2, so it is only necessary to find the coordinates of the intersection point of these two lines. Set the right-hand sides of the two equations equal: 2x-1=(3/4)x+3/2. Moving terms gives 2x-(3/4)x=3/2+1, that is, (5/4)x=5/2, so x=2. Substitute into y=2x-1, obtaining y=2×2-1=3. Therefore the coordinates of point A are (2,3).
